slides.title: Is dark roast stronger coffee?
slides.subtitle: It depends on what you mean by strong.

slides.myth: Dark roast is stronger than light roast
slides.truth: Not in caffeine. Measured by weight, light and dark roasts hold about the same. What changes is the taste.

slides.title: Strong means two things
slides.body: Strong flavor means bold, smoky, intense. Strong caffeine means how much caffeine ends up in your cup. Dark roast usually wins the first one. It doesn't win the second.
slides.highlight: Bold taste is not extra caffeine.

slides.title: What roasting really changes
slides.body: Heat darkens the beans and builds roasty flavors. Lighter roasts usually taste brighter and fruitier. Darker roasts usually taste bolder, with less of that tangy note.

slides.title: Why scoops can mislead
slides.body: Roasting dries the beans and makes them puff up. A scoop of dark roast usually weighs a bit less than a scoop of light roast. Weigh your coffee in grams and the gap mostly disappears.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Choose by taste, not by color. Want it bolder? Try a darker roast. Dose in grams, so every cup is comparable.

slides.title: Dark roast is bolder, not stronger
slides.body: Roast changes the flavor. The caffeine stays about the same.
slides.cta: Share with a dark roast fan
